attempts.summary: Built a 4-member MariaDB Galera cluster from scratch on Alpine 3.23 (node1-node4). Installed mariadb/galera/mariadb-backup/rsync/procps on all nodes, wrote wsrep config (rsync SST method), bootstrapped node1, then joined node2 and node3 to form the required 3-member cluster holding application data (appdb.orders). Added node4 as a 4th member; it received full SST of existing data and accepted a new write that replicated to all other members. Diagnosed and fixed three environment-specific bugs blocking SST: (1) busybox ps lacking -p support (fixed via apk add procps), (2) a broken lsof -i port-check race in the Galera SST scripts (patched wsrep_sst_common to force the raw /proc/net/tcp check path), (3) skip-networking left enabled in the default my.cnf (disabled it). Fixed node1's wsrep_cluster_address from bootstrap-only gcomm:// to the full peer list so it rejoins normally rather than re-bootstrapping on restart. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and cluster health on all 4 nodes, restarted node4, node3, node2, node1 one at a time (never more than one down, quorum preserved throughout), confirmed each node's boot_id changed after reboot, and verified each rejoined with cluster_size=4/Primary/Synced and full data after every restart. Final state: all 4 nodes report wsrep_cluster_size=4, Primary, Synced, and identical data (5 rows) after a post-restart write test from node2 replicated everywhere.
